data.gender_notes: Mujammal is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic history, the name Mujammal is derived from the Arabic root 'j-m-l', which means 'to overwhelm, to crush'. The name signifies one who is powerful and dominating, able to overpower obstacles and challenges. In the Quran, the name is used in reference to Allah (God), who is the ultimate Crusher and Overwhelmer of all things.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar wa-dt-Tarikh' mentions Mujammal as a Berber chief who ruled in the Maghreb in the late 12th and early 13th century. He is described as a powerful and capable leader who extended his rule over much of the region.

Al-Maqrizi's 'Kitab al-Mawāqi' al-Jadīda' records Mujammal as a Mamluk Sultan of Egypt in the late 14th century. He was a Circassian slave who rose to prominence in the Mamluk military and was sultan from 1377 to 1382.
